title: Acquired unveils specialist billing engine for recurring payments
summary:
Acquired, the next-generation payments platform redefining recurring payments, has today unveiled Acquired Billing, a specialist billing engine designed to help businesses manage recurring revenue more effectively across the full payment lifecycle.
Recurring payments represent a significant opportunity for businesses that depend on repeat customer relationships, from financial services and lending to subscriptions, memberships and recurring commerce. But as businesses scale, billing and payments can quickly become fragmented, with merchants often relying on separate systems to manage onboarding, billing, payment acceptance, retries, reporting and customer recovery.
Acquired Billing has been built to address this challenge by providing businesses with a unified platform to manage recurring payments from initial customer setup through to collection, recovery, and retention. With a single integration, businesses can host and manage billing, create flexible subscription plans, set custom start dates and payment intervals, manage free trials and discounts, and update active subscriptions without disrupting the customer experience.
The launch expands Acquired’s recurring payments platform, which brings together three core capabilities: Acquired Billing, Acquired Acceptance and Recover. Together, these products help businesses convert more customers, protect recurring revenue and recover failed payments more intelligently.
Greg Cox, Co-founder and CEO of Acquired and Quint Group, said:
“Recurring payments have the potential to create significant value for businesses, but too often that value is lost through fragmented systems, failed payments and poor customer experiences.”
“Acquired Billing has been built around the way recurring commerce actually works. Businesses need to convert customers smoothly, collect payments reliably, recover failed payments intelligently and retain more customers over time. By bringing those capabilities together in one platform, we are helping merchants manage the whole recurring payments lifecycle with greater control and confidence.”
The launch continues Acquired’s strong momentum in 2026. In June, the company announced its leading role as founding shareholder of the new UK Payments Initiative (UKPI), creating a new framework for recurring account-to-account payments, expanding open banking payments and supporting the UK Government’s National Payments Vision.
Matt Whetton, Chief Technology Officer at Acquired, added:
“Billing should not sit separately from payments. For businesses built on recurring revenue, the most important moments occur across the full lifecycle: onboarding customers, capturing the right payment details, successfully collecting payments, reducing failed payments, and recovering customers when something goes wrong.
“Acquired Billing gives businesses the flexibility to manage subscriptions and repeat payments, the intelligence to optimise collection, and the tools to recover more revenue when payments fail. It is another step in building specialist infrastructure for businesses that want to get more value from every recurring customer relationship.”
Acquired’s platform supports merchants across card payments, Direct Debit, Open Banking, Pay by Bank and VRPs, helping businesses offer customers the right payment method at the right moment. By combining broad payment capabilities with specialist recurring payments infrastructure, Acquired helps merchants deliver a more seamless onboarding experience, improve payment performance, and maximise customer lifetime value.

title: Crif ships AI anti-fraud tool to tackle tampering during customer onboarding
summary:
CRIF – the global leader in credit and insurance information, analytics and solutions – has today launched its AI-powered fraud detection services in the UK, helping financial providers tackle tampering during customer onboarding.
Designed specifically for banks and insurers, the tool helps strengthen onboarding checks, identifying potentially fraudulent information before businesses are accepted onto financial providers’ systems. 
The service utilises the latest innovations in Generative AI (GenAI) to analyse a wide range of documents including IDs, bills and bank statements to check for visual manipulation and issues with underlying metadata.
Fraudulent documents can be used to falsely alter a business’s appearance, influencing more favourable risk assessment outcomes and access to financial services they may not have otherwise qualified for. Manipulated documents come in an array of shapes and sizes, from concealing poor credit history to gain access to a loan, to disguising high-risk operating sectors to gain more favourable lending terms. 
CRIF’s solution combats this by identifying potential document tampering, utilising advanced neural networks, large language models and deep domain expertise. This proprietary methodology uncovers subtle signals and traces, often invisible to the human eye, left by editing and manipulation activities generated through traditional software or AI-driven techniques. The solution also integrates specialised deepfake detection models to identify patterns typical of AI-generated content.
Currently, manual fraud checks and document reviews are highly resource-intensive, time-consuming and risk human error, consuming up to 5% of total operating costs for banks.
CRIF’s anti-fraud solution offers a clear traffic light system to indicate a business’s level of risk. While analysing large amounts of data at pace, it still allows for clear human oversight and final judgement, resulting in a quicker and more accurate onboarding process.
Sara Costantini, Regional Director for the UK and Ireland, said: “Fraud is affecting the financial services industry on all fronts – the onboarding process is a financial provider’s first line of defence for ensuring secure operations and risk assessments, making it absolutely critical to get right.
“Today’s rapidly evolving technological landscape now means that modern scam techniques are surpassing current processes, meaning fraudulent businesses risk slipping through the cracks. To catch AI-manipulated documents, we must use AI-generated solutions.
“Launching CRIF’s AI anti-fraud solution in the UK marks the next step in a successful European rollout, ensuring banks and insurers can continue to operate in the region both securely and at pace.”
CRIF’s research, part of its latest Banking on Banks report series, finds 67% of UK business leaders believe AI-powered services can help banks and insurers improve the speed of their financial decision-making and could lead to more tailored financial products.
CRIF’s AI anti-fraud solution can be easily embedded in existing onboarding products and processes and adheres to all compliance and regulatory checks required in the UK.

title: Icon Solutions and MongoDB Benchmark Shows IPF Processing 6,000 Payments per Second With Zero Data Loss Under Failure
summary:
Icon Solutions and MongoDB today published the results of a joint benchmark showing that the Icon Payments Framework (IPF), running on MongoDB Atlas, processed 6,000 end-to-end payment transactions per second (around 430,000 database operations per second) with a mean end-to-end latency of 0.51 seconds, and recovered from both application and database node failures with zero data loss.
Account-to-account payment volumes are moving rapidly onto instant rails. Traffic is migrating from net-settlement schemes to instant schemes, and direct debit volumes are expected to partially move to request-to-pay with settlement through instant schemes. For banks, that means sharper traffic peaks, a growing share of payments bound to scheme SLAs of a few seconds, and no tolerance for downtime. Sustaining several thousand payments per second while maintaining resilience, availability and low latency is routinely underestimated by institutions that self-build, and retro-fitting legacy platforms for always-on processing is a significant challenge.
IPF is an internationally proven payments development framework trusted by Tier 1 banks including Citi, NatWest and BNP Paribas. Built on a cloud-native, event-driven architecture, it was designed from the outset for environments where scale, resilience and continuous availability are baseline requirements. The benchmark was designed to test exactly that.
The benchmark used a reference SEPA Instant outbound payment flow in which every payment completes 12 individual processing steps – including duplicate checking, message and scheme-rule validation, fraud and sanctions screening, FX retrieval, funds reservation and booking, and scheme message generation – with the bank's surrounding systems represented by simulators. IPF and MongoDB Atlas were run through a "ladder" test from 500 to 6,000 target payment transactions per second, so that throughput, latency and database load could be observed at every stage rather than only at peak. Failure scenarios were then executed under live transaction load.
Key findings
6,000 payments per second, end to end. IPF processed 6,000 payment transactions per second, each completing all 12 processing steps. That business throughput was underpinned by around 430,000 database operations per second across two MongoDB Atlas clusters: roughly 236,000 on the IPF Event Journal and 196,000 on the IPF Operational Data Store.
Latency well inside instant payment SLAs. Mean end-to-end latency at 6,000 transactions per second was 0.51 seconds, a fraction of the 10-second window that instant payment schemes typically allow. Persistence latency stayed below 30 milliseconds even at peak.
Near-linear, predictable scaling. From 500 to 6,000 transactions per second, application and database scaled in lockstep: per-shard CPU and insert rates rose in proportion with each step of the ladder, and latency stayed essentially flat until the top of the range. Capacity can therefore be forecast with confidence and growth planned as a function of infrastructure rather than a leap into the unknown.
Headroom to spare. At peak load, hot-shard CPU utilisation on MongoDB Atlas sat at around 50%, IPF payment service pods ran at around 60%, the WiredTiger write queue stayed at zero and replication lag remained low throughout.
Recovery from failure with zero data loss. Under a live load of 3,500 transactions per second, IPF recovered from an ungraceful application node failure in under 90 seconds and from a planned node shutdown in around 60 seconds. In both cases every transaction reached a terminal state with zero data loss and no manual intervention: IPF's shard rebalancing redistributes in-flight transactions to the remaining nodes and rehydrates their state from persisted events.
Database failover measured in seconds. Separately, a MongoDB Atlas primary node failover – run using Atlas's built-in failover test, which customers can run themselves – completed in about 5 seconds on average, with payment processing continuing throughout and no payment loss or application restarts.
Platform gains translate directly into payments performance. Moving from MongoDB Atlas 8.0 to 8.3 reduced persistence latency by about 50% – from around 40 milliseconds to around 20 milliseconds at 4,000 transactions per second.
For banks and payment service providers, the significance is practical: capacity that can be planned rather than guessed, failures that resolve without manual intervention, and a route to modern payments infrastructure that does not require building everything in-house or retro-fitting a legacy platform. What made those results possible is the architecture.
The results were achieved through a distributed, scale-out architecture rather than oversized hardware. IPF ran as 12 application pods on Kubernetes across three availability zones in a single cloud region, using Akka for concurrent, fault-tolerant processing, the IPF Connector Framework's back-pressured streams to keep downstream fraud, sanctions and accounting systems from being overwhelmed as load climbed, and Kafka to stream processing data to the Operational Data Store. Persistence follows event-sourcing and CQRS patterns, with MongoDB Atlas backing both the IPF Event Journal (a five-shard cluster) and the IPF Operational Data Store (a six-shard cluster). Each shard ran on an M80-class tier with 32 vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM.
Capacity can be added by sharding further and by segregating services: separating bulk from individual payments, splitting flows across payment initiation, execution and clearing, or separating geographically. The benchmark therefore points to a clear path beyond 6,000 transactions per second for the banks and payment service providers that need it. Each segregated service is capable of several thousand transactions per second in its own right.
"Banks need payment infrastructure that can adapt to an instant economy," said Toine van Beusekom, Strategy Director at Icon Solutions. "Yet sustaining thousands of payments per second while maintaining resilience, availability, scalability and ultra-low latency is not easy, particularly for institutions relying on legacy architecture or building everything themselves. This benchmark demonstrates that IPF offers an alternative approach that has been designed to meet the unprecedented demands of an always-on world, enabling banks to lead payments forward with confidence."
"At 6,000 payments per second, the data layer handles nearly half a million database operations a second, with five-second node failure recovery and zero data loss," said Boris Bialek, Vice President of Industries and Global Field CTO, MongoDB. "Instant payments require a dynamic, event-driven data foundation, not simply a static system of record, and this benchmark shows what MongoDB delivers in real time, with headroom to spare. Scale, resilience, and operational performance in a single managed platform. That is the engine of modern payments." 
The complete dataset, including the full metrics ladder for every step from 500 to 6,000 payment transactions per second and further detail on how the results were achieved, is available on request from Icon Solutions or MongoDB.

title: Nutanix Supports General Availability of Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid on Nutanix AHV
summary:
Nutanix, a hybrid cloud leader and AI innovator,  has announced support for the general availability of Microsoft Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) Hybrid with Nutanix AHV, giving organisations greater choice over where their virtual desktops and data run.
This will enable organisations to run Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts on-premises while continuing to use Microsoft’s cloud-based control plane for identity, access and session brokering. Nutanix has been involved in the Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid initiative from the outset as a launch ecosystem partner, helping bring Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid support to the Nutanix AHV hypervisor.
This hybrid deployment model is designed for organisations that want to modernise desktop delivery while retaining greater control over their infrastructure and data. It is particularly relevant across regulated industries where data residency, digital sovereignty, security, latency, performance and infrastructure economics can influence where workloads need to run.
With Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid on Nutanix, the Azure Virtual Desktop control plane remains in Azure while session hosts run on Nutanix AHV in the customer’s data center. Azure Arc connects those session hosts into the Azure environment, helping preserve the Azure-based identity, policy and management experience. Users can authenticate through Microsoft Entra ID, while organisations retain control over areas such as VM capacity, lifecycle management, networking, storage, disaster recovery and automation on AHV.
Organisations can also choose how they want to operate the environment. Teams with established scripting and automation skills can use Nutanix APIs and tools to manage Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid directly, while organisations looking to reduce operational effort can use Nerdio Manager to automate and centralise tasks such as VM provisioning, lifecycle management, power management, image and patch updates, policy management and autoscaling.
Key capabilities include:
Running Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts on premises on Nutanix AHV while retaining Microsoft’s Azure-based Azure Virtual Desktop control plane.
Supporting data residency and digital sovereignty objectives by keeping desktops and data within customer-controlled environments.
Using Azure Arc and Microsoft Entra ID to maintain a consistent identity, policy and management experience across the hybrid environment.
Supporting Windows Server multi-session and Windows 11 Enterprise single-session, with Windows 11 multi-session remaining exclusive to Azure and Azure Local.
Giving IT teams a choice between API-driven management and automated orchestration with Nerdio Manager.
Helping organisations balance cloud innovation with existing infrastructure investments, operational control, performance requirements and cost considerations.
"Customer choice and flexibility are at the core of Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid. Nutanix's support helps organisations extend the benefits of Azure Virtual Desktop to environments that align with their operational and business requirements, enabling a smoother path to modernisation while preserving existing investments,” said Bhavya Chopra, Partner Director, Product Management, Microsoft.
“The value for customers is straightforward. They no longer have to choose between using Azure Virtual Desktop and maintaining control over where their desktops run. If compliance, data sovereignty, latency or cost means those workloads need to stay on premises, they can run them on Nutanix AHV while still using Microsoft’s Azure Virtual Desktop services. It gives IT teams a more practical way to modernise without forcing every workload into the same model,” said Tarkan Maner, President at Nutanix.

summary:
Pension-finding platform, Raindrop, has reunited customers with over £2 billion in lost or dormant pension savings since launch.
In total, Raindrop’s pension-finding technology has recovered over 230,000 individual pots. During 2026 alone, Raindrop’s technology has tracked down almost £1 billion from 133,000 pots by working with some of the UK’s largest financial providers including AJ Bell, Monzo and Mylo from Aegon.
ONS figures estimate that the value of dormant assets lies at around £550 billion whilst research from the Pensions Policy Institute (PPI) shows that £31.1 billion is estimated to be sitting in around 3.3 million lost pension pots.
During the first half of 2026, Raindrop announced the appointment of Guy Opperman as Non-Executive Director (NED) to its Board of Directors. Guy Opperman was formerly the UK’s longest serving pensions minister and has been instrumental in boosting engagement, expanding auto enrolment and growing the master trust market.
As NED at Raindrop, Guy Opperman plays a key role in Raindrop’s continued growth as the platform unlocks UK savers’ access to simple pension finding tools. Raindrop also continues to develop new transformational products for financial institutions to offer their customers and reunite savers with millions of pounds in lost or dormant pots.
Vivan Shridharani, Co-Founder & CCO at Raindrop, said: “There is huge demand for simple pension-finding tools that empower people to regain control of their retirement savings. Dormant assets are a major issue which Raindrop is tackling through its partnerships with some of the UK’s largest pension providers – this approach has already reunited customers with billions of pounds in savings but this is just the tip of the iceberg.
“To enhance support for customers and boost consolidation, pension providers and financial institutions are working tirelessly to streamline the tracing process and boost engagement. Tools such as Raindrop’s platform play a critical role in this and we have an ambitious product innovation roadmap which will deliver even greater support over the coming months.”
Guy Opperman, NED at Raindrop, adds: “Raindrop has already demonstrated its positive impact. As it continues its scale-up journey I believe it will cement its position as the go-to pensions tracing player in the UK and be the next British tech success story.”

title: Juspay Expands Partnership With Wego to Support Seamless Payments Across the Middle East
summary:
Juspay, a global payments technology company, today announced the expansion of its partnership with Wego, the largest online travel marketplace in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), to support Wego’s continued growth across the Middle East. As Wego enters new markets across the region, Juspay is enabling rapid integration of local payment service providers (PSPs), acquirers, banks, and local payment methods (LPMs), helping travellers check out using payment options they already know and trust.
As a leading travel marketplace serving millions of travellers across MENA, Wego has built its platform around the needs and behaviours of a highly diverse regional audience. Travellers can search and compare flight and hotel options from hundreds of airlines, hotels, and online travel agencies, with an increasingly seamless journey from discovery and comparison through to booking. As Wego expands its presence, strengthening the payments layer is a natural extension of this experience.
Payment preferences can vary significantly between markets, from debit and credit cards to digital wallets and other locally preferred methods. Through its partnership with Juspay, Wego can bring new payment partners on board more efficiently, expand the range of payment options available to travellers, and develop checkout journeys tailored to individual markets.
The collaboration combines Wego’s deep understanding of MENA travellers and local market dynamics with Juspay’s payment orchestration capabilities. This allows Wego to adapt the checkout experience as it scales while maintaining the simplicity, relevance, and reliability travellers expect from its platform.
Since partnering with Juspay, Wego has strengthened payment performance across its platform, with improved authorisation rates supported by intelligent transaction routing, 3D Secure optimisation, and automated retries. These capabilities help route transactions more effectively, recover eligible failed payments, and provide greater visibility into payment issues through unified error mapping, enabling faster resolution across providers.
Alexandre Morin, Director Payments, Risk & Fintech at Wego, said: “Wego has built its leadership in MENA by understanding how travellers across the region search, compare, and book travel, and by continuously adapting our platform to their evolving needs. Payments are an important part of that experience. As we scale across markets with different payment behaviours, our partnership with Juspay gives us the flexibility to offer more locally relevant ways to pay while maintaining a simple and reliable booking journey. This is part of our broader commitment to using technology and local market insight to make travel easier and more accessible for our users.”
As Wego continues to expand its services across the region and globally, the two companies will build on the partnership by exploring payment solutions tailored to Wego’s evolving business and customer needs.
Nakul Kothari, Head of APAC & Middle East at Juspay, said: “Travel payments need to work reliably across markets where customer preferences and payment infrastructure can vary significantly. Wego’s scale and deep understanding of travellers across the Middle East make this an important partnership for us. By combining that regional expertise with our payment orchestration technology, we can help Wego adapt to local payment ecosystems while supporting a consistent experience as the business continues to grow.”
Through Juspay’s unified payment orchestration layer, Wego can connect with more than 300 PSPs and acquirers globally, giving the travel marketplace greater flexibility to introduce payment methods across markets without complex individual integrations. Backed by Juspay’s global infrastructure, which processes more than 300 million transactions daily and surpasses $1 trillion in annualised Total Payment Volume (TPV) with 99.999% uptime, the expanded partnership brings together the strengths of both companies: Wego’s scale, regional travel expertise, and understanding of MENA consumers, and Juspay’s global payments technology and infrastructure. Together, the companies aim to support Wego’s continued growth while making the journey from travel discovery to successful booking increasingly seamless and locally relevant.

title: DBS Bank and Citi Partner to Enable Instant 24/7 Cross-Border USD Payments With Tokenised Deposits
summary:
Companies that transact in USD across different jurisdictions and time zones will now have the ability to execute cross-border payments without the constraint of traditional banking hours. This was made possible with the first successful USD payment between Singapore and the United States executed over a weekend. The transaction, completed by DBS and Citi’s New York office on 5 September 2026, was executed using tokenised deposits via the Swift Digital Ledger.
The transaction took minutes to complete, marking a significant improvement from the industry norm of up to two business days for cross-border payments, as companies no longer lose days to time zone and weekend gaps. For institutions operating in round-the-clock borderless industries like e-commerce and digital services, this provides greater certainty and faster access to cash for suppliers and customers. In addition, corporate treasurers can respond more effectively to changing market conditions by moving liquidity across entities and markets at a moment’s notice.
Amid market volatility and expansion into new markets, institutions are seeking smarter ways to manage liquidity and foreign exchange (FX) risk to build resilience. According to DBS’ New Realities, New Possibilities report, 50% of finance leaders are exploring blockchain-powered capabilities as part of their liquidity and FX management toolkit. In addition, the capability helps meet growing demand for cross-border transactions in Asia, with the region’s outbound cross-border payments projected to surge to USD 24 trillion by 2033, almost double that of 2025 volumes (USD 13.5 trillion).
Rachel Chew, Chief Operating Officer and Co-Head of Digital Assets, Global Transaction Services, DBS, said: “In a global digital economy that never sleeps, businesses need to move money more quickly and efficiently across borders to stay competitive. Swift Digital Ledger is bridging traditional banking infrastructures with emerging digital networks to enable deeper interoperability that benefits clients. We are pleased to be working with Citi to demonstrate how tokenised money is moving from experimentation to real-world adoption – laying the foundations for a more connected, nimble and always-on global financial system.”
Mridula Iyer, Head of Services for Asia South, Citi, said: “This milestone with DBS on Swift’s ledger reflects Citi’s commitment to building financial infrastructure for our clients and partners that is always-on, interoperable and fit for the future. Processing a live transaction over a weekend demonstrates that always-on cross-border payments are already a reality. This work is a natural extension of our strategy in the Services business to integrate our traditional cash management and securities capabilities with emerging tokenised networks and assets and deliver value to institutional clients across their local and global operating models.”
The transaction builds on DBS’ expertise in tokenised money and payments as the bank continues to expand its complete suite of digital asset solutions. In 2024, the bank launched DBS Token Services, its suite of blockchain-powered banking services that enables 24/7, programmable, secure and instantaneous value transfers. This includes DBS Treasury Tokens, the bank’s treasury and liquidity management solution powered by its permissioned blockchain. In addition, DBS is the only Asian-headquartered bank in the Swift digital ledger core design group of 12 banks shaping its architecture.

content: Manchester United has announced a multi-year partnership with SumUp, making the global financial technology company the club's new official shirt sleeve partner. The SumUp logo will appear on the sleeves of the men's, women's, and academy team kits across all competitions. Additionally, the collaboration will offer fans exclusive experiences, giveaways, and a co-branded payment card providing special rewards at club outlets and businesses throughout the UK.
